title: The Neighbour: ricercar a 4 on the pipe organ (Bach version)
about: The four voices on the Norrfjärden Church organ (audio/organ), one division each so the lines stay apart in colour and position: soprano on the Hauptwerck, alto on the Oberwerck, tenor on the Rückpositief, bass on the Pedal (16'+8' as its floor). In the arioso the soprano takes the Rückpositief Krummhorn as a solo and the tenor moves to the Hauptwerck Gedackt; both return at 35. Dynamics are terraced: the registration changes only at section and entry joins, each division at a point where its own voice attacks (no stop is drawn under a held key), never as a hairpin. Because each voice has its own division, a join can lift only the voice that carries the entry (41 and 43: the soprano's inversion; 55-57: the tune as a cantus firmus on the Principal over flutes). Principal chorus built 8', 8'+4', 8'+4'+2' through the fugue; plenum with pedal reeds for Climax I (26:3), Climax II (52:1; manual reeds and the Quintadena 16' added at the fff peak 53:1) and the apotheosis peak (59:1: the tune on the Hauptwerck plenum with Trommeten over the answer in the pedal reeds); flutes for the subito-piano spans (arioso accompaniment, fuga inversa, the dominant pedal) and under the coda's d''. The augmented inversion in the pedal (46-55) gains the 4' at 48 and the reeds at 52. The Oberwerck's own plenum draws the Spitzquinten 1 1/2', whose recorded pipes beat (audio/organ/README.md, Limits), so the alto's chorus registrations are custom lists without it. gain_db balances the divisions as recorded (K-weighted stem levels on this piece: the Oberwerck sits about 3 dB and the Hauptwerck about 1.5 dB under the Rückpositief at the same tier). Rendered by render.sh: orchestrate.py (plan.json, this spec; integrity check), articulate.py (baroque touch), render_organ.py with the church acoustic, qa_organ.py and presence.py.

changes.why: I exposition, p to mp: the tune alone on the Principal 8'; the answer on the Quintadena with its 4' flute
entry 4, mf: the tenor's answer and the alto's CS2 step up; the soprano's descant stays on the Principal 8'
episode, mp: the first terrace down (an echo); the alto attacks at 18:1
the tenor's G3 is held to 18:1.5, its next attack
stretto, the false dawn, building to f
liquidation and Climax I, ff: plenum, pedal reeds under the heads on E, G, B-flat, D-flat; all four attack at 26:3
II arioso dolente, subito pp: the soprano's S2 as a Krummhorn solo on the Rueckpositief over the alto's Quintadena and the tenor's Gedackt
III fuga inversa, pp: the inversion enters alone in the pedal
A minor established: + 4'
third entry, the inversion in the soprano: only its division steps up (principal 8'+4'), the others stay on flutes 8'+4'
mf into the A-minor cadence 45:3: the soprano's inversion on 8'+4'+2', the tenor on principals
IV the dominant pedal, subito p misterioso: the augmented inversion in the pedal under the tenor's lament
combination, mp: S2 (alto) and S1 (tenor) together, their divisions up a step; the pedal's 4' brings out the augmented inversion
towards f; the soprano enters at 50:3 with the heads in diminution (three speeds: diminution, S1 in the tenor, the augmentation in the pedal)
Climax II: C major, the light; every voice attacks at 52:1
fff peak: the complete C7, manual reeds (Trommeten, Schalmei, Krummhorn) and the Quintadena 16'
the hinge, f to p: first step down
V apotheosis, p: the whole tune in B-flat major as a cantus firmus on the Principal 8' over flutes 8' (CS2 in the tenor, the free alto) and the lament in the pedal
mf: only the tune steps up (principal 8'+4')
apotheosis peak, f at 60:4: the tune's second half on the plenum with Trommeten over the answer in the pedal reeds
towards mp: every voice attacks at 61:3
p: c'' rises to d'' over V7-I and the tolling tonic pedal
coda, pp: the inner voices on flutes 8' under the soprano's d'' on the Principal 8'
the alto's F4 is held to 65:3
